business_problem: Horizon needed to scale training, storage and network infrastructure for mass-market autonomous-driving programs as shipments, partner vehicle programs and model-training workloads grew quickly.
solution_summary: Horizon expanded its autonomous-driving infrastructure with Baidu AI Cloud so it could support a much larger volume of training and data operations for the Journey family of ADAS platforms. The program focused on three layers. For storage, Baidu optimized the底层 architecture and provided EB-scale BOS object storage plus high-performance parallel file storage to handle heavy ingest and read/write requirements from large training jobs. For compute orchestration, Baidu helped Horizon build a very large CCE container cluster that can run more than 100,000 pods and manage 10,000-card-class GPU resources in a unified pool, improving utilization and operational control. On the networking side, multiple dedicated links and bandwidth expansions were added to keep large-scale training and cross-cloud flows stable. Horizon and Baidu also co-developed automated GPU fault detection and handling so problems could be resolved in minutes instead of becoming long-running operational bottlenecks. This created a shared backbone for ongoing autonomous-driving training, storage and compliance work.

data_flow: Autonomous-driving datasets are stored in BOS and parallel file storage, scheduled into large training jobs across the container cluster and GPU pool, and then circulated back into Horizon's model-development and compliance workflows as new vehicle programs scale up.
business_outcome: Horizon secured a more scalable and resilient infrastructure base for autonomous-driving training, improved compute efficiency and positioned itself to support a much larger number of vehicle programs and shipments.
